rationale: Excluded under E01 (wrong topic). This systematic review examines greenhouse gas emissions, energy/carbon footprints, and decarbonization technologies and policies in the food and beverage industry. Aside from a passing background mention of industrial/supply-chain water consumption as an environmental impact of food and beverage consumption, it does not examine household or community water or sanitation service access (Criterion 1) or water/sanitation access outcomes (Criterion 4).
plain_vs_narrow_note: Although the review mentions generic policy options and institutional barriers for industrial decarbonization (satisfying a literal unanchored reading of Criterion 2, though failing the narrow water/sanitation rule-type reading), it clearly fails Criterion 1 and Criterion 4 because it studies food and beverage industry greenhouse gas emissions rather than household or community water or sanitation service access. Both readings therefore result in exclusion (E01).

evidence_quotes.quote: Decarbonizing the Food and Beverages Industry: A Critical and Systematic Review of Developments, Sociotechnical Systems and Policy Options

This paper presents a comprehensive, critical and systematic review of more than 350,000 sources of evidence, and a short list of 701 studies, on the topic of greenhouse gas emissions from the food and beverage industry.

It examines the benefits to sector decarbonization—including energy and carbon savings, cost savings, and other co-benefits related to sustainability or health—as well as barriers across financial and economic, institutional and managerial, and behavioral and consumer dimensions.
